short: All three changed components are standard: on-device few-shot head untested against prototypes or fine-tuning; voiced enrollment loses 5.6 points; visual KWS predates it uncited.
position: LipLearner [@su2023liplearner] changes command registration (M03), enrollment from a voiced utterance (M01) and activation by visual keyword spotting (M06); all three are standard. Its frozen-encoder linear head is the only one among 30 few-shot vocabulary studies (pattern match, Appendix), but the one-shot 25-command F1 of 0.8947 over 1,000 random draws (§5.3) faces no prototype or fine-tuning head (§5.2–5.4). The voiced-to-silent loss (87.29% against 81.67%, §8.2.2) is the known overt-to-silent degradation, and KWS activation is new only for lipreading interfaces, as the paper says (§6.1): visual-only spotting predates it uncited [@momeni2020seeing; @stafylakis2018zeroshot]. The superiority claim rests on an in-house counterpart trained from scratch (0.9895 against 0.7147 F1, §5.4).
